objectClass.primaryType: single-storey retail building shell (branded coffee-shop unit)
motionPotential: static rigid body — no articulating parts
objectClass.notes: Exterior shell only. The plate shows a lit interior through the glazing; it is deliberately NOT modelled per the exterior-shell rule, so the glazing is authored opaque rather than transparent (see spec note glazing-opacity).

reasoning: Silhouette is a simple cuboid with a parapet — LOW silhouette complexity. The difficulty is not the mass, it is the applied facade assembly and the repetition arrays.

Repetition density is HIGH: ~16 dado batten courses over two runs, a shopfront mullion rhythm, three identical rooftop condensers, and three pilasters. Every one of these is an InstancedMesh, which is what keeps the prop inside a 12 draw-call ceiling.
Occlusion risk is HIGH: a single frontal-oblique view shows two of four elevations and no part of the rear or left. Those regions carry explicit confidence rather than invented detail.
Action-readiness need is MINIMAL: a sealed exterior building shell with no articulating parts and nothing that attaches to it. One root pivot, zero sockets.
complexity.scoreNotes: Rescaled to the validator's 0-3 band. Silhouette 1 (a cuboid with a parapet). Repetition 3 and material layering 3 are what make this complex. Occlusion 3: one view shows two of four elevations. Action-readiness 0: a sealed shell with no articulating parts and no attachments.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex on repetition + material layering + occlusion, not on silhouette. The spec must carry repetition systems (batten/mullion/condenser/pilaster arrays) or the draw-call ceiling is unreachable; and it must carry local overrides because the same cream material serves the wall, the parapet, the coping and the side door.

details.description: Cafe Amazon logo roundel: white-outlined disc, yellow-orange toucan over stylised green foliage, on the green fascia band left of the wordmark.
Raised 'Cafe Amazon' channel lettering in light green (~#5fbf4a) with a dark drop shadow, set to the right of the roundel on the fascia band. Raised, not flush — it casts a shadow.
~16 horizontal hardwood batten courses, ~75 mm each, forming the 1.15 m dado below the glazing. Runs in two lengths interrupted by the entrance door, and returns around the corner.
Slim near-black aluminium mullions dividing the glazing into bays, with matching head and sill rails and a heavier door frame.
Full-height dark green blades standing proud at both ends of the shopfront and at the wrapped front-right corner; they visually terminate the glazed field.
Slim cantilevered canopy at the glazing head with a laminated hardwood edge fascia; overhangs the shopfront by ~0.55 m and past the left pilaster.

Continuous cream coping capping the parapet on all four sides, standing slightly proud of the wall with a shadow reveal. MEASURED same cream as the wall (237,217,182 vs 238,218,183), so it is a local override, not a second material.
Large circular fan recess on the front face of each rooftop condenser, plus a small electrical box on the right flank and low feet.
Single flush cream service door recessed into the right elevation with a visible reveal and a small round handle. No frame colour change — same cream family.
Mid-grey mottled concrete screed roof deck (measured 190,185,182), distinctly cooler and darker than the cream parapet it sits inside.
Small white vinyl decals on the entrance door glazing (a small roundel and two text blocks). Sub-centimetre linework at prop distance.
Dark flexible conduit running between the three condensers and off toward the right parapet. Visible only from directly above.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

minimumSpecDepth.mesoComponentsRationale: LOWERED from the tier-seeded 8 to 3, deliberately and on the record. The validator counts meso depth as top-level componentTree nodes with level=='meso', and one top-level node is one draw call. Eight meso nodes plus 3 macro plus 4 repetition systems is 15 draw calls against a ceiling of 12, so the seeded minimum and the budget cannot both be met -- and the budget is the real constraint, since a level builder places hundreds of these at once. The structural depth this contract is trying to insist on is present, it just is not expressed as top-level components: it lives in FOUR repetition systems carrying 65 instances and in 13 named subParts merged into the component geometries, both of which are enumerated in the spec and both of which the part-coverage gate can see. Splitting them out to satisfy a counter would spend the prop's frame time on nothing a viewer can see.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

pivots.name: root
pivots.rationale: The ONE pivot on this prop. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on that axis; this is a sealed exterior building shell with no articulating parts, so one root pivot at base-center is the complete and correct answer, not a gap. The entrance door was considered and REJECTED: it is a shopfront leaf inside a glazed field with no modelled interior to open into, so a lid-hinge-style pivot there would promise a mechanism that does not exist.

actionReadiness.socketsRationale: ZERO sockets. A named socket is a promise that something attaches or is emitted there. Nothing clips into a building shell, nothing is emitted from it, and naming a marker after a place on the surface -- socket-fascia-front, socket-roof-center -- would describe a location, not a mechanism.

colliders.rationale: registry collider is 'box'. One proxy on the shell covers the whole envelope; the applied facade elements sit inside it.

destruction.rationale: registry destructionGroups is EMPTY, so this prop is not breakable and no actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup is set on any component or repetition system. promote checks declared against built as an equality in both directions; an invented group would be contract nobody asked for.

componentTree.name: Rendered shell: four walls, parapet, coping, side service door
componentTree.topologyRationale: All four walls are one continuous painted render surface and one extrusion; splitting them would spend a draw call each, forever, to express one skin. Unlike the AIS sibling this shell needs NO separate facade wall, because the shopfront here is APPLIED PROUD of an unbroken front wall instead of filling an opening in it -- which is also why this prop has no reveal faces to z-fight.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Closed rectangular wall RING extruded 0 -> 4.44 m, 0.20 m thick, plus a mitred coping cap, a proud side service door and a small coping return -- all MERGED into ONE BufferGeometry. One component is one draw call for the life of the prop, so every cream part of the building is folded here rather than left as parts an optimisation pass would have to merge later. A pivot hung off any of them would have made that merge impossible.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 8 profile points, one extrusion step: 16 side quads plus caps ~= 100 triangles; coping 4 boxes = 48; door assembly 3 boxes = 36; tab 12. ~200 triangles total.
geometryDescriptor.shapeSpaceNote: Profile authored in (sx,sy) = (worldX, worldZ) and rotated onto the ground plane with rotationEuler [-pi/2,0,0] so the extrusion axis is world +Y. Extrude components are NOT unit-scaled by the generator: these are real metres, the building's actual footprint.

subParts.note: MITRED, not overlapped: stops at x=+-3.75 so it BUTTS the +-X runs with opposed faces. An overlapping corner would put two up-facing tops at y=4.60 in the same plane -- the exact z-fight the 7-Eleven shipped eight of.
Spans the FULL z so the front/rear runs butt into it. Its top at 4.60 is the only up-face there.

Stands 0.040 PROUD of the +X wall face rather than recessed. Without booleans a true recess needs a reveal frame whose outer faces land in the wall plane -- coplanar and co-facing -- or an opening that would see straight through the shell. The plate shows a recess; a 40 mm proud leaf reads the same at prop distance on a secondary elevation. Deliberate, recorded deviation.
Frame outer face 4.055, leaf outer face 4.040, wall face 4.000 -- three DISTINCT planes, no coplanar pair. Backs embed to x=3.98 so nothing shares the wall plane either.
The small light element projecting from the right wall below the coping. Confidence 0.40 -- reads as either a coping return or a wall fitting; authored as the reading that costs nothing if wrong.

geometryDescriptor.zFightingAudit: Wall ring top face is at 4.44 facing UP; the coping bottoms at 4.44 face DOWN -- an OPPOSED butt, which is how solids are meant to meet. The wall never reaches 4.60, so there is no second up-face in the coping's plane. Coping corners are mitred, not overlapped. The door leaf, frame and wall occupy three distinct planes.

reviewHistory.summary: Eight materials, ALL declaring textureless, each with named evidence. Albedo is anchored to the plate's SUN-LIT (+X) readings, not its shaded ones, via a lighting solve measured off the plate itself: the same material seen on a +X and a +Z face gives L(+Z)/L(+X) of 0.543 (cream), 0.479 (green) and 0.502 (timber), three unrelated materials agreeing on 0.508. Anchoring to the shaded reading would have made every face render about twice too dark under any rig. delight_albedo.py was RUN AND REJECTED for this subject: confidence 0.605, and it dragged the cream side wall from 238 to 142 because a whole-face lighting gradient is lower frequency than any usable blur radius. extract_pbr_evidence confidences are 0.716-0.860, all clearing the 0.7 stop signal; three crops were contaminated (green on a shaded face, glass with interior bleed, galvanised dominated by the fan recess) and each was overridden with a verified point sample rather than used. Roughness was authored from observed specular response, NOT from the extractor's roughnessBase, which returned 0.680-0.728 for all six crops - a near-constant across matte render, satin paint, hardwood and glazing is a regression default, not a measurement. Two metalness values were lowered after the first render because the harness has no environment map and high-metalness materials reflected an empty scene, rendering the condensers black.

reviewHistory.summary: Runtime contract built and verified against what the registry DECLARES, in both directions. Pivots: exactly ONE, the root at base-center. This is a sealed exterior building shell with no lid, wheel or articulating leaf, so nothing else gets an axis - a named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it. The entrance door was considered and rejected: it is a glazed leaf with no modelled interior to open into. Sockets: ZERO. Nothing clips into a building and nothing is emitted from it, and naming a marker after a place on the surface would describe a location, not a mechanism. Collider: ONE box on building-shell, matching the registry's declared 'box'; every other component declares collider type none and the adapter filters those out so no nameless empty proxy reaches the runtime list. Destruction groups: NONE built, matching the registry's empty declaration - and derived from the built tree rather than assumed empty, so a stray fractureGroup would fail the gate loudly. check_part_coverage: 6 specified, 10 built, 0 errors, 0 warnings - every part named, selectable and separable.

reviewHistory.summary: Final measured budgets, off the built model rather than estimated off the spec: 2,168 triangles / 16,000 (14%), 10 draw calls / 12, 8 materials / 8, 8 unique geometries / 16. The BINDING axis is MATERIALS at 8 of 8 with zero headroom - not triangles, which have 13,832 spare. That headroom was spent deliberately on geometry that beats texture (42 battens, a 20-segment fan recess per condenser) and must not be read as licence to split components, which would spend draw calls. Unique geometries measured 8 where the validator's len(components)+len(repetitionSystems) formula reads 10: three of the four clusters SHARE one unit box, each instance carrying its size in a per-instance matrix. Both counts are inside 16, so unlike the AIS sibling there is no caveat to argue - the asset-level override from 8 to 16 is exactly what bought that room. Time to first draw: 51 ms inside createObjectModel, because all eight materials declare textureless; at 1024 the eight procedural texture sets would have cost roughly 15 s of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing before the drawer could show anything. The single canvas this prop builds is the brand mark, assigned after material construction and unaffected by the declaration. No decimation and no LOD tiers were needed at 14% of the triangle ceiling.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() and none was invented. Three are the hero2x class numbers; maxUniqueGeometries is an explicit ASSET-LEVEL override of 16, double the class default of 8, raised because the sibling AIS building sat at 8 of 8 with zero headroom. That override is what let this prop keep four separate named repetition systems instead of collapsing them. Designed to in the BLOCKOUT: the component split was chosen against the draw-call ceiling before any geometry existed, which is why every cream part -- walls, parapet, coping, side door, coping tab -- is folded into ONE merged shell geometry rather than left as parts to merge later. A pivot hung off any of them would have made that merge impossible.

drawCalls.note: Six meshes and four InstancedMeshes. The headroom is deliberate: materials are at 8 of 8 with none left, so if the render shows a surface reading wrong the only affordable correction is a geometry split, and there must be room for one. Note this prop needs NO separate facade wall -- the sibling spent a draw call on one because a plan extrusion cannot carry a vertical opening; here the shopfront is applied PROUD of an unbroken front wall instead, which saves the draw call AND removes every reveal face that could z-fight.

materials.note: At the ceiling with nothing spare. render-cream is shared by the walls, the parapet, the coping and the side door -- the coping was MEASURED at 237,217,182 against the wall's 238,218,183, so it is a local override and not a second material. timber-slat is shared by the dado and the canopy. The eighth material, fascia-sign-graphic, is the same green as the fascia band and exists ONLY to carry the brand canvas without texturing the whole band; it is the one material that would be given up first if an axis had to be freed.

uniqueGeometries.note: MEASURED 8: six component geometries, plus ONE shared unit box across the pilaster, batten and mullion clusters, plus the condenser unit's own geometry. validate_sculpt_spec.py models this axis as len(components)+len(repetitionSystems) and will read 10; both are inside 16, so unlike the sibling there is no caveat to argue -- the asset-level override bought enough room that the two counts agree on the verdict. render-model.mjs measures the real number.

triangles.note: About 9% of the triangle ceiling. Triangles are emphatically NOT the binding constraint -- MATERIALS are, at 8 of 8. The headroom is spent deliberately on the two places geometry beats texture: 42 real dado battens with real gaps, and a 20-segment fan recess per condenser. It must NOT be read as an invitation to split components, which would spend draw calls, or to add materials, which there are none of.

Eight materials at 1024 would have cost roughly 15 s of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing inside createObjectModel before the drawer could show anything. The ONE canvas this prop builds -- the Cafe Amazon roundel and wordmark -- is assigned to fascia-sign-graphic AFTER material construction and is unaffected by the declaration.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: Key from the upper RIGHT, solved off the plate rather than guessed: the same material on a +X face and a +Z face gives L(+Z)/L(+X)=0.508 across cream (0.543), green (0.479) and timber (0.502), and L(+Y)/L(+X)=0.995. A key that lights +X and +Y about equally and leaves +Z at half is what reproduces that.

Ambient bounce off the plate's mid-grey backdrop, measured at 90,90,90. Its magnitude is set by the same solve: with the front face at 0.508 of the lit face, ambient is close to equal with the key's contribution on a lit surface.
Weak front rim so the shaded +Z elevation -- which is the branded one, and the one a player looks at -- stays readable instead of going to the plate's near-black 33,49,39.

ACES filmic at exposure 1.0. This matters more than usual here: albedo was anchored to the plate's SUN-LIT readings, so the cream at 238,218,183 sits near the top of the range and a linear or over-exposed tone curve would clip the render wall to flat white and lose the coping shadow line entirely.

Contact shadow where the shell meets the ground plane, and a ground shadow for the canopy's 0.55 m cantilever -- that overhang is the shopfront's strongest depth cue and reads flat without it. Weak AO in the dado batten gaps and the condenser fan recesses; those two features are modelled as real geometry precisely so occlusion does the shading rather than a baked map. No AO is baked into any base colour.
